label: Zimmermann 1778 introduces major human variation as Abartungen oder Varietäten after a plasticity demonstration
subject: work.zimmermann-geographische-geschichte-vol1.1778

sources.citation: E. A. W. von Zimmermann, Geographische Geschichte des Menschen, und der allgemein verbreiteten vierfüssigen Thiere, vol. 1 (1778), pp.53-60; ETH-Bibliothek/e-rara record 6943987, image-page ids 6944061-6944068

observations.value: p.53: humans endure extraordinary, almost unbelievable changes of climate and nourishment before the main variation catalogue begins
p.59: Nach dieser Vorbereitung ... zu den Abartungen oder Varietäten des Menschengeschlechts
p.59: the greatest varieties are to be shown as durch Klima und Nahrung möglicher Weise hervorgebracht; the argument establishes causal possibility, not a complete factual history
Abartung and Varietät are coordinated by oder at the entry point and are not defined there as separate nested ranks

claim_limit: Do not infer perfect synonymy in every occurrence of Abartung and Varietät across the volume, or a fixed rank hierarchy from this entry passage.

label: Zimmermann 1778 represents bodily colour as gradable and hypothetically time-indexed
subject: work.zimmermann-geographische-geschichte-vol1.1778
object: visible human colour between white and black

sources.citation: Zimmermann 1778, vol.1, pp.106-108; ETH-Bibliothek/e-rara image-page ids 6944114-6944116

observations.value: p.106: Nüancen ... große Verschiedenheit, oder vielmehr Stufenfolge; nature passes nach und nach toward the Negro
colour is represented by shades/stages rather than discrete self-contained bins
p.108 asks how much Schwärze might increase in each century under a given climate
climate plus duration is proposed as a mechanism capable of altering visible colour

claim_limit: The blackness-per-century formulation is a hypothetical research calculation, not an observed quantitative law and not evidence of a stable hereditary essence.

label: Zimmermann 1778 gives climate explicit jurisdiction in division into human races
subject: work.zimmermann-geographische-geschichte-vol1.1778
object: Abtheilung des Menschen / Zerfällung in verschiedene Racen

sources.citation: Zimmermann 1778, vol.1, pp.108-111, especially p.109; ETH-Bibliothek/e-rara image-page ids 6944116-6944119

observations.value: p.109: bey der Abtheilung des Menschen, oder bey seiner Zerfällung in verschiedene Racen mehr auf das Klima Acht zu geben
Zimmermann immediately treats Blumenbach's four Hauptracen as a relevant partial implementation
visible bodily difference motivates classification, but climate is assigned organizing authority beyond simple political-continent or colour mapping

claim_limit: Do not paraphrase this as climate alone defining race, or as modern ecological population genetics; migration, mixture, inheritance and other causes remain active in the same argument.

label: Zimmermann 1778 permits a Race to arise historically from inherited family peculiarity plus non-mixture
subject: work.zimmermann-geographische-geschichte-vol1.1778

sources.citation: Zimmermann 1778, vol.1, pp.100-105; ETH-Bibliothek/e-rara image-page ids 6944108-6944113

observations.value: European parents with a persistent inherited bodily peculiarity could, if they remained unmixed, produce a Race marked by that trait
a separated family forced to marry within itself could eventually produce a wunderbare Menschenrace
Zimmermann explicitly says he is not certain that important historical Abartungen actually arose this way; he claims the mode is possible

claim_limit: This establishes a possible race-generating mechanism, not the actual historical origin of any named major race and not a modern genetic definition.

label: Zimmermann 1778 treats migration and mixture as interference with clean racial classification
subject: work.zimmermann-geographische-geschichte-vol1.1778

sources.citation: Zimmermann 1778, vol.1, pp.107-108; ETH-Bibliothek/e-rara image-page ids 6944115-6944116

observations.value: p.107: Zerfällung des Menschengeschlechts is made difficult by Völkerwanderung and the resulting Vermischungen
present political continents and current population distributions cannot be read as transparent natural divisions
mixture can delay or complicate the climatic production of expected bodily forms

claim_limit: Do not infer that Zimmermann rejects classification; he seeks a more natural causal-geographical principle while admitting historical mixture obscures it.

label: Zimmermann 1778 separates visible colour, causal possibility, race formation, historical reconstruction and classificatory warrant

sources.citation: Primary-controlled clusters: pp.31-34, 53-60, 100-111, 114-115, Zimmermann vol.1 (1778), ETH-Bibliothek/e-rara record 6943987

observations.value: measured environmental intensity -> plasticity / causal possibility -> gradable visible difference -> reproductive and migratory population history -> classificatory grouping
möglicher Weise, mathematisch gewiß and Einfall mark repeated distinctions between causal sufficiency and actual historical certainty

colour is descriptively salient, gradable and causally transformable, but does not by itself authorize essential group membership; its classificatory meaning is embedded in climate, duration, inheritance, migration and mixture
Meiners later operates in much of the same causal field but more explicitly regulates taxonomic rank and admissible bodily evidence

claim_limit: Do not infer direct Zimmermann-to-Meiners textual dependence without citation/contact evidence. The claim is a structural comparator, not a genealogy of influence.
